title: Booking Europe, setting a standard and George Wein
summary: Hodes explains how Harriet Choice, George Wein and two bookers got him to Europe. He says one should set a standard fee.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I get to Europe because of him. And there's two fellows that are booking singles that hear me. That's the sequence of events. So they heard me and they says, hey, man, will you come over for me? So that means three weeks working in Europe, three and a half. There's a man in England that won't book me, unfortunately. Now, he's booking all these other people, but to tell you the truth, he won't pay me what I can get going to Germany for this other man. He just -- I don't know what, in Europe he says, England is a poor country. I don't know what they're getting paid, I really don't. But it takes a certain amount. You set a standard. You say I want so much money. And if you don't get it, you don't say to a man, what will you give me? When you start that kind of nonsense, you're lost.
So you set a standard. You lose some and you win some, is the way I figure it. I've just set a standard. I'm

not higher -- I've talked to different musicians, and I know I'm not getting what Joe Venuti or Red Norvo would have gotten. But I'm getting what I think is a fair sum to bring me over there. I'm not living in the same house I have, I have to live in a room where there's just a shower and no bathtub, or some -- things like that. There's no place to eat in the room. After work, everything is closed.
